report.summary: Cross-slice review of shard 19 finds no contradictions, but several files have CLAIMS without corresponding symbols (shift_hook, arch_hook, shift_ticker, providers/base, langgraph_adapter), making those claims unverifiable. Orphans: crew_hook.py UNWIRED as a whole, and backward-compat re-exports in ikarus.py. No duplicated responsibility or clear missing edges detected.
risks: Overstated claims: daedalus/shift_hook.py, daedalus/arch_hook.py, daedalus/shift_ticker.py, daedalus/providers/base.py, daedalus/langgraph_adapter.py have CLAIMS but no symbols in the census, so their guarantees cannot be validated.
Orphans: daedalus/crew_hook.py is completely UNWIRED, and backward-compat aliases in ikarus.py (Ikarus, MetronScheduler, etc.) have no internal dependents, risking accumulated dead code.
Missing census coverage: the absence of symbols for files appearing in READS/CLAIMS suggests incomplete shard data, weakening structural confidence.
todos: Complete symbol listing for shift_hook.py, arch_hook.py, shift_ticker.py, providers/base.py, and langgraph_adapter.py to validate claims.
Deprecate or remove crew_hook.py if confirmed unused.
Audit ikarus.py re-exports for external consumers; consider deprecation.
Revisit the eval package claim about distilled slices; ensure it is backed by run_tier1/run_tier2.

handoff.suggestion: Re-run census for the noted files to capture their symbols. Investigate crew_hook.py and ikarus.py usage. Downgrade claims for files with no supporting symbols until evidence is provided.
